## labs/nvidia/pixelumm

PixelUMM - Encoder-free unified image and video understanding and generation in one model.

Status: deferred. Install: none. Artifact: source-build. Arm64: unknown. GB10: unsupported. Comfy shape: none.
Input: text, image, or video
Output: generated image or video
Licenses: code Apache-2.0 with file-specific exceptions. Weights Hugging Face card tagged license:other, terms not read. Commercial use unknown.
Footprint: 240 GB VRAM, 200 GB disk. Weights: nvidia/PixelUMM/S8-F*-R*/*.distcp@121.6, Qwen/Qwen3-8B/model-0000*-of-00005.safetensors@16.4.
Artifact ref: https://github.com/nv-tlabs/PixelUMM.git
Upstream: https://github.com/nv-tlabs/PixelUMM
Also: https://huggingface.co/nvidia/PixelUMM
Sources: https://github.com/nv-tlabs/PixelUMM

Nothing in this graph touches the GPU. The row's work runs outside the Comfy process through the operator CLI, so the App claims no occupancy and stops no heavy job: the one-heavy-job rule is the CLI's to enforce, next to the heavy confirm and the headroom preflight.

Operator verbs (host shell):
  bazelisk run //:manage -- nvidia-lab status
  bazelisk run //:manage -- nvidia-lab plan pixelumm

Canvas:
1. Preflight prints whether this Spark could run the row today - the catalog row, an aarch64 host, the binary that row's install kind needs, and the artifact ref.
2. The verdict card prints the blocking reason and the sentence that would reopen the row.
3. The tier table prints all 18 rows with their status and licenses.

Gate notes: The released weights are 121.6 GB of distributed checkpoints and the documented training path asks for seven GPUs of 48 GiB or more. That is a cluster, and this stack is one Spark. The weight terms on the card are license:other and were not readable as a permission for product use.
Reopen: A quantized single-GPU inference checkpoint with a readable permissive weight license.
Verify: bazelisk test //tests:bats_nvidia_lab_test

Occupancy: none - stop nothing GPU. One GB10 job.
